author: ttravis786
body:
#### PR description:

This PR adds a neural-network (NN) common-mode (CM) correction for HGCal rechits as an energy variation, alongside the existing linear-regression correction. Layer clusters (LCs) get the corresponding energy and time variations. This only adresses the 222 channel LD modules, future models will handle both HD and LD modules.

Some relevant links:

Details on the model: https://indico.cern.ch/event/1718533/#sc-8-8-noise-mitigation
Details on the CMSSW validation: https://indico.cern.ch/event/1731004/#18-dnn-based-common-mode-subtr
Details on the PR: https://indico.cern.ch/event/1748250/#7-ongoing-developments-for-coh

The NN runs alongside the nominal reconstruction and is stored only as an alternative: nominal `energy`, zero suppression and clustering still use the linear CM correction. The producer parameter `useCMML` itself defaults to `false`, and when it is off no model is loaded and CM_ALT equals `energy`.We'll implement the usage of this producer in a full workflow in the coming weeks - for the moment we would need this as an integrated code basis.

```
    energy                       = EM*MIPS * ((adc - ADC_ped - CM_lin) - BXm1_slope*(adc_m1 - ADC_ped - CM_lin))
    energy_variations(CM_ALT)    = EM*MIPS * (adc - ADC_ped - NN)    (no BX-1 term)
    energy_variations(SCALE_ALT) = energy                            (placeholder)
```

CM_ALT falls back to `energy` for TOT hits, invalid digis, unconnected cells, modules without 222 channels, or `useCMML=false`.

This PR:
1. collects the 254 NN input features using alpaka kernels
2. runs the NN inference in `HGCalRecHitsProducer` through PyTorchAlpaka
3. appends the energy variations to rechits, and the energy and time variations to LCs

Two models are available, `zscore` (default) and `plain`, set through the `model`, `modelManifest` and `inputPreprocessing` parameters. `cmAltAsNominal` (default false) swaps the two corrections, so the NN drives zero suppression and clustering.

Data format changes:
- `HGCalSoARecHits`: `energy_variations`
- `HGCalSoAClusters`: `time`, `energy_variations`, `time_variations`
- `HGCalSoAClustersExtra` (workspace columns)
- `HGCalSoARecHitsProducer`, which converts legacy rechits to SoA for the alpaka layer clustering

Layer clusters:
- `time` is new: the energy-weighted mean of member rechit times, with weights max(E, 0), using rechits with time > 0, and -99 if the weights sum to 0.
- `energy_variations` are re-summed from the member rechits. There is no re-clustering, and positions are not varied.
- `time_variations` use the same rechit times with varied weights. Rechit times are not recomputed with the varied energy, so their timewalk correction still uses the nominal energy.

Fixes to existing layer-clustering code:
- `HGCalSoARecHitsLayerClustersProducer`: the cluster count was uninitialised for events with no rechits, which caused a crash. It is now zeroed and CLUE is skipped for empty input.
- Position kernels: a cluster with no member with E > 0 made the kernels read rechit index -1, which aborted the job. Such clusters now get x = y = z = 0.

Dependencies (needed for this PR to work in a release):
- https://github.com/cms-data/RecoLocalCalo-HGCalRecProducers/pull/5: NN models, their manifests and preprocessing, and `cellareas.json`. Needed when `useCMML=True`.

Supersedes #52109.


#### PR validation:

This had been validated and presented in the HGCAL DPG + HGCAL Test Beam groups. If interested in the methodology for testing, + also how to reproduce the tests see below.

Physics validation used CMSSW_20_1_0_pre4, el9_amd64_gcc14, TB2025 run 112049.

1. Each incremental change was run on 20 events, checking that the NN inputs and the CM_ALT energies of rechits and LCs did not change.
2. Before each push, a full run (107 < trig_time < 113, `knoise=-100`) was processed and the noise peak fitted over [-10, 10] ADC, on connected cells. The fit mean and width were checked to be unchanged, and they match Arne Reimers' offline results from training and evaluating the models.

 Full recipe: https://gitlab.cern.ch/hgcal-dpg/hgcal-comm/-/work_items/53#note_12627512

Not a backport, and no backport is planned.
title: HGCAL: Introducing DNN-based Common Mode noise subtraction for HGCAL
